newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Aer Lingus calls reports of job cuts "speculation".
newsitem.headline: Aer Lingus calls reports of job cuts "speculation".

text.p: Irish national airline Aer Lingus said on Wednesday newspaper reports that it was planning to cut between 500 and 700 jobs as part of a cost-cutting programme were speculation.
But it added that "cost reduction is central to any future viability for the airline."

"Aer Lingus finances are still fragile and we must continue to reduce our operating costs," the airline said in a statement. "If we are to stay in business and have a commercial future that is the only way forward."

A joint working group comprised of management and staff was currently examining options to ensure future viability, Aer Lingus said, adding that substantial savings had already been targeted and this had been communicated to staff.

Irish union SIPTU sad it was "outraged" by reports of job cuts. "Workers should not be treated in this way -- SIPTU will oppose any further job cuts in Aer Lingus," said Paul O'Sullivan, SIPTU senior negotiator at Aer Lingus.
"The company has acted in appalling bad faith," O'Sullivan said in a statement, adding that the union had "now lost all confidence in the current senior management".
SIPTU said it was seeking an urgent meeting with transport minister Michael Lowry, where it would demand a guarantee that there would be no job cuts.
The Irish Independent newspaper said Aer Lingus was planning a new cost cutting programme which would seek to reduce costs by 20 percent through job cuts and productivity gains.

SIPTU accused Aer Lingus of planting the story in the media. "The senior management who planted this story in the media must be made accountable for their actions," O'Sullivan said. "At no stage have the company's representatives given any information on the plans reported in today's paper."
But Aer Lingus insisted staff would be the first to hear of any planned job cuts.
"Future plans, in so far as they impacted on employment in the company, would in the first instance be communciated to the staff and their representatives," it said.
Aer Lingus' last major restructuring programme was the Cahill plan in 1993, which involved the loss of 1,200 jobs.
